entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Manius Acilius Glabrio Gnaeus Cornelius Severus, a senator of the Roman Empire, played a significant role in shaping the empire's governance during the 2nd century CE. Born into a prominent family, he rose through the ranks to become consul ordinarius in 152 CE, alongside Marcus Valerius Homullus.

Glabrio's tenure as consul was marked by his efforts to maintain stability and order within the empire, which was facing internal conflicts and external pressures. His leadership during this period was instrumental in ensuring the continuation of Roman dominance in the region.

Despite his notable achievements, Glabrio's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by the more prominent figures of the Roman Empire. Nevertheless, his contributions to the empire's governance during this critical period make him an important figure in the history of the Roman Empire.

Glabrio's impact can be seen in the continued stability and prosperity of the Roman Empire, which would go on to shape the course of Western civilization for centuries to come.
